_comment: Example global data in the format the server sends. Places are real Gainesville parks, but the amenities, descriptions and trail routes are made up / approximate for testing. Trails here use gpx_file (relative to this file); the server sends the GPX text as gpx. The John Muir Trail (trails/John_Muir_Trail.gpx) is from OpenStreetMap via waymarkedtrails.org. Hawthorne-trail locales are fictional and snapped onto the track in trails/Gainesville-Hawthorne_State_Trail.gpx. The server starts with this file; to change a running server's copy: python server.py --load-global global/global_data.json

locales.name: Depot Park trailhead fountain
locales.description: Bottle-fill fountain at the western trailhead; potable

locales.name: Boulware Springs spigot
locales.description: Spigot behind the restroom building; potable, may be off in winter

locales.name: Prairie Rim primitive site
locales.description: Two tent pads under live oaks overlooking the prairie; no water, pack it in

locales.name: Sweetwater cistern
locales.description: Rain cistern with tap; untreated, filter or boil

locales.name: Prairie Creek bridge camp
locales.description: Fire ring and picnic table near the creek bridge; creek water must be treated

locales.name: Rochelle crossing hand pump
locales.description: Well hand pump at the County Rd 234 crossing; tested potable

locales.name: Lochloosa Pines group site
locales.description: Group site for up to 12, pit toilet, bear-proof food box

locales.name: Lochloosa Creek access
locales.description: Natural source below the boardwalk; tannic, filter before drinking

locales.name: Hawthorne trailhead overflow camp
locales.description: Grassy overflow field near the eastern trailhead; register at the kiosk

locales.name: Hawthorne trailhead spigot
locales.description: Potable spigot next to the eastern trailhead kiosk

trails.name: Gainesville-Hawthorne Trail
trails.description: Paved rail trail from Depot Park east past Boulware Springs

trails.name: John Muir Trail
trails.description: Yosemite Valley to Mount Whitney through the Sierra Nevada; most of it is also the Pacific Crest Trail
